newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond futures rollover proving tame.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond futures rollover proving tame.

text.p: The Australian bond futures market is currently going through the quarterly ritual of the rollover of contracts, but the switch to December from September is proving a fairly tame affair this time round, traders said.
The September three and 10-year bond contracts close-out at midday on Monday.
"It seems to be going smoothly. The 10-year looks about fair value, the three-year looks a bit expensive, but I don't suspect any problems," said one trader at a European based bank.
The spread between September and December 10-year contracts has held between 4.5 and five basis points for most of the week.
The three-year, meanwhile, has banded in a seven to eight basis point spread range.
"The open interest on the 10-year contract was relatively low, so this is why the rollover has been fairly orderly," another trader added.
The market has seen several spells of heavy liquidation in the past two weeks, particularly from computerised trading accounts (CTAs), as the market corrected the steep rally between June and August.
In that time the September contract soared from 90.800 to 92.210, its highest level in almost 2-1/2 years, but is now currently trading at around 91.905.
The December contract was at 91.865 at 2.05 p.m. (0405 GMT).
